Still present in v1.14.24 — and the scope is broader than described         

The original report covers the case where a provider is absent from enabled_providers. I hit a more severe variant: the package is loaded and blocks the event loop even when the provider is completely absent from opencode.jsonc — not just filtered, but not defined at all.

Setup: headless opencode serve on macOS, desktop app on a second machine connecting over LAN.

Repro:
1. Add a custom npm provider (e.g. @ai-sdk/openai-compatible) to the config and run npm install in ~/.config/opencode/
2. Remove the provider block from opencode.jsonc entirely (empty "provider": {})
3. Start opencode serve
4. Server receives requests but /session never starts processing — event loop is blocked

Finding: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible sitting in node_modules is enough to trigger the blocking load. The config is irrelevant. The only fix is npm uninstall @ai-sdk/openai-compatible in ~/.config/opencode/.

The proposed fix in this issue (if (!isProviderAllowed(providerID)) continue) would fix the enabled_providers case but likely not this one — the loader seems to scan node_modules independently of config. Might be worth tracing where that scan originates.

That's the nuance — when using the built-in DeepSeek provider (which sets `capabilities.interleaved = true`), PR #24146's fix works fine. But when using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` as a generic adapter, the model definition lacks both `interleaved` and `reasoning` capability flags, so `normalizeMessages()` never enters the `reasoning_content` injection branch.

The user's opencode.json model config may be correct, but the AI SDK's `convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages()` doesn't add `reasoning_content` to history messages (it only emits `reasoning_content` when `reasoning.length > 0` at the SDK layer). So even with a proper model definition, the replay path still drops it.

Our fix (PR #24150 / commit b5b6ad05d on our fork) approaches this at `normalizeMessages()` level — unconditional injection of `reasoning_content: ""` for any model that has either `interleaved`, `reasoning` capability, or any existing message with reasoning parts in the conversation. This covers the generic adapter case without requiring model-config-level changes.

Hey everyone! 👋 While we wait for the official fix to get merged, I built a workaround plugin [opencode-enforce-context-mode](https://github.com/AbdelrhmanUZaki/opencode-enforce-context-mode) so you can still use `context-mode` properly despite the `session.created` bug.

It solves the problem using two steps:

1. Proactive Guidance: It bypasses the broken hook by using experimental.chat.messages.transform to inject the environment constraints directly into the first user message, so the AI knows to use ctx_* tools immediately.

2. Aggressive Enforcement: If the AI still attempts to run a forbidden native command (like grep or curl), it gets blocked by a fatal system directive that forces immediate compliance and redirects it to the correct context-mode alternative.

If you're using `@ai-sdk/openai`, the change doesn't apply (different code path).

Our fork has the full fix at commit `b5b6ad05d` (https://github.com/fkyah3/opencode-fkyah3/commit/b5b6ad05d) that covers both layers:
1. `provider.ts` — enable interleaved for reasoning models (included in this PR ✅)
2. `transform.ts normalizeMessages` — unconditional `reasoning_content: ""` injection for ALL assistant messages (NOT in this PR, needs separate PR)
